deferred_classes.microkinetic: CatMAP / Cantera backend is conda-only; runs under pixi (see NEXT_STEPS.md)

report.transition: Phase 2 — explicit electrochemistry attributes the limitation of carbon fixation at the mineral interface

feasibility.admissibility: grid points where every runnable class ran to completion with its charge ledger closed; favorable = settled throughput >= 10% of the class's own maximum (open flow, dilution as swept)

robustness.note: fraction of the swept grid (uniform in log over the vg-data priors, NOT a conditioned posterior) that is favorable; structure_agreement = fraction of the region both classes call favorable on which they agree about the limitation label (the failure-mode-attributed gate metric)

proposed_perturbations: measure the current-voltage curve of the wall (polarization): the Butler-Volmer class predicts an activation-dominated cell whose current scales with the exchange current, the empirical class a pmf-saturating drive; the two differ in how throughput responds to a 10x catalyst change
vary the wall conductivity across 1e-7..1e-5 S/m: both classes predict the electrical collapse there, so the location of the knee calibrates the layer thickness / conductivity product
run the microkinetic class under pixi (CatMAP / Cantera) to test whether site coverage and passivation move the catalytic label toward transport at high current
discrimination.note: paired standardised difference d between model classes on identical grid points

report.headline: Phase 2 — explicit electrochemistry attributes the limitation of carbon fixation at the mineral interface: predicts under stated assumptions; feasible=yes (93/375 admissible parameterizations support it); robustness=0.25 of the posterior (agreement across classes 0.47); most discriminating readout: log10_throughput (d=10.99)

decision_discipline: model classes disagree on most of the posterior; conclusion is structure-sensitive, cannot be called necessary
